evals.prompt: Are we ready to launch? PR #412 adds a `loyalty_points` column to `customers`, backfills it from order history, and shows points on the checkout page. Going to 100% of users Thursday. Load test hit p99 180ms against a 250ms target (link: grafana/d/lt-412). We have a dashboard but haven't added alerts yet. Support hasn't been told.
assertions: Lists 3-5 failure modes specific to this change (e.g. backfill load on customers, wrong point totals shown at checkout) before the checklist
Every check row has a status of met, not met, or n/a with a reason, plus an evidence column and an owner expressed as a role
Rollback is the first row and is not met, because no tested rollback or data story was supplied
Detection is not met because no alerts exist, and the report hands off to observability-plan rather than drafting the alert inline
The quality-targets row is met and cites the supplied load-test link as evidence
Exposure is flagged because a 100% launch is not staged and no reason is given for why all-at-once is safe
The verdict is BLOCKED, and the reason given is the missing rollback
No dashboards, test results, or sign-offs are invented beyond what the prompt supplied

evals.prompt: We're switching on SMS 'ready to collect' reminders across Brightwell Pharmacies on Monday. Everything is in launch-brief.md, load-test-summary.txt, privacy-signoff.txt and sms-template.txt. I need to tell the steering group on Friday that we're green. One page please.
assertions: Does not say the launch is green; it recommends not launching on Monday as planned until the named problems are fixed
Catches that the load test only sustained 1,200 messages per minute, with rate limiting above 1,250, against an expected peak of 1,500, which contradicts the brief's 'tested at 3x peak'
Catches that the SMS template includes the medication name, which the privacy sign-off explicitly does not approve
Catches that turning the flag off does not undo migration 0042, which drops patients.reminder_opt_in, so the stated rollback is not a full one
Notes that no alerts exist yet and that switching on all 140 stores at once leaves no staged rollout
Does not invent evidence, owners' names, dates or test results that are not in the files
Fits on one page

evals.prompt: we run a small yoga studio and we're turning on online class booking tomorrow. the guy who set it up says it's all done. are we ready? what should I check before tomorrow? short list please
assertions: Does not declare the studio ready, because nothing has been shown beyond the setup person saying it is done
Gives a short checklist, not a long report
Includes trying a real booking from start to finish, including payment and a cancellation or refund
Includes a fallback for if the booking system fails on the day (for example taking bookings by phone or on paper) and telling customers about the change
Uses plain language a studio owner can follow
Does not invent details of their booking system, prices or policies
